body.p: (task 0.7). The substrate is five headers, each including only those before it: name.h (name pool) < types.h (type registry, sequence types, node kinds) < tree.h (tree interface, node references, axes, tree builder, arena tree) < xdm.h (item heap, items, sequences, atomic items, node items, function items, maps, records, arrays, JNodes). tree.h forward-declares sxml_item_heap; status.h already declares sxml_sequence, which xdm.h defines. Accessors that produce XDM values from nodes (string value, typed value, base URI) are in xdm.h; structural accessors in tree.h. There is no "processor" object in the substrate: the name pool, type registry and item heap are separate objects with stored references (heap -> registry -> pool), and the Phase 1 processor owns them. Document and collection resolution (fn:doc, fn:collection, fn:unparsed-text, module import) is a host interface of the dynamic context, designed with it in Phase 1, not a substrate header: what it returns (a tree made through sxml_tree_builder, or bytes) is already covered here.
